geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
Practice the lessons so far, then check your answers.

Goal: I can apply inequality theorems and parallel tests.

  • 5.1 I can use properties of inequality in proofs.
  • 5.2 I can prove an exterior angle is greater than either remote interior angle.
  • 5.3 I can order sides from angles and angles from sides, and prove the perpendicular is the shortest segment from a point to a line.
  • 5.4 I can decide if three lengths form a triangle.
  • 5.5 I can compare sides of two triangles with two equal sides.
  • 5.6 I can prove lines are parallel from equal corresponding or alternate interior angles (using the exterior angle inequality).
  • 5.8 I can state the Parallel Postulate and explain why it is a postulate.
  • 5.9 I can prove angle relationships formed by parallel lines and a transversal.
  • 5.10 I can prove interior angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees.
  • 5.11 I can prove an exterior angle equals the sum of the remote interior angles.
  • 5.12 I can prove AAS and HL using the angle sum, and explain why HL needs a right angle.
  • 5.13 I can decide if lines are parallel, perpendicular, or neither from slopes or equations (used computationally here; proved in 9.10).
  • 5.14 I can write an equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line through a point.
  • 5.15 I can combine parallel lines and congruence in a proof.

slides.title: Practice: 5.1
slides.html: If x > 7, what can you say about −2x?
slides.reveal: −2x < −14. Multiplying by a negative number reverses the inequality.

slides.title: Practice: 5.4
slides.html: Two sides of a triangle are 5 and 9. What lengths can the third side have?
slides.reveal: Any length between 4 and 14, not including 4 or 14.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html:
Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • the longest side can be anywhere
  • any three lengths make a triangle
  • the converse of a parallel-line theorem is the same theorem
  • HL works for any triangle
  • perpendicular slopes are just "negatives"
